claim:walk-forward.proposition:
The evolved walker travels ~450 units over a 500-step trial and never
reverses, taking 25 regular steps — a sustained forward walk, not a one-off
lunge (which a pure-distance fitness produces, reaching only ~21).

claim:cpg-limit-cycle.proposition:
The evolved CTRNN's state traces a clean closed loop in its activity space — a
limit cycle — repeating once per stride (~19.8 steps). The rhythm is a
self-sustaining attractor, not a clocked or scripted sequence.

claim:gait-and-velocity.proposition:
A regular gait: stride period 19.8 ± 0.4 steps (the spread is only ~2% of the
period), duty factor 0.44 (stance and swing nearly balanced), mean body
velocity ~9.0 units/time (~0.9 units/step).

narrative.question:
Can a small continuous-time recurrent neural network, coupled to a single
leg over flat ground, evolve into a central pattern generator that produces
a rhythmic walking gait — a self-sustaining stance/swing cycle that carries
the body steadily forward — rather than a one-off lunge?
